slot.brief: Binomial situation: given n and p (as fractions), compute mean and/or variance of the distribution; single-formula numerical.

stem: A random variable $X$ has a binomial distribution with $18$ trials and success probability $\dfrac{5}{9}$. Its mean and variance, respectively, are

verdicts.working: For a binomial variable, mean = np = 18(5/9) = 10 and variance = np(1-p) = 18(5/9)(4/9) = 40/9.

working:
$p=\dfrac{5}{9},\quad q=1-p=\dfrac{4}{9}$
$\mathbb E[X]=np=18\cdot\dfrac{5}{9}=10$
$\operatorname{Var}(X)=npq=18\cdot\dfrac{5}{9}\cdot\dfrac{4}{9}=\dfrac{40}{9}$

Independent check: For a binomial variable, mean = np = 18(5/9) = 10 and variance = np(1-p) = 18(5/9)(4/9) = 40/9.
solution:
For a binomial distribution, $\text{mean}=np$ and $\text{variance}=npq$, where $q=1-p=\frac49$.
$$\text{Mean}=18\frac59=10,\qquad \text{Variance}=18\frac59\frac49=\frac{40}{9}$$
